item.title: Browser Run - Chrome 152 and Quick Actions improvements
item.description:
• Upgraded the default browser to Chrome 152.
  • The default User-Agent for Quick Actions now reports Chrome 152 instead of Chrome 119. If you allowlist or match the Browser Run User-Agent, update your rules. Refer to Automatic request headers.
  • Quick Actions requests now look more like requests from a regular Chrome browser, so fewer sites block them.
  • Pages that return large response headers now load correctly.
  • Removed distrusted root certificates from the Browser Run trust store.
  • /links now returns absolute URLs, and links-only crawls now follow relative links.
  • /markdown and crawl Markdown output now keep code block languages.
  • Quick Actions that time out now return a consistent error, and outbound Workers that throw an exception now return an HTTP error to the browser.

item.title: Browser Run - Browser binding session and DevTools methods
item.description:
• Browser Run browser bindings now support typed methods for acquiring and connecting to sessions, launching a browser with outbound Worker routing, creating Live View URLs, and managing session lifecycle.
  • Added a nested devtools binding with methods for browser version and protocol information, listing and creating targets, and activating or closing targets. See the Browser binding API reference for the full API.

item.title: Browser Run - Structured handoff for Human in the Loop
item.description: • Human in the Loop now supports structured handoff using Cloudflare-specific CDP commands. Your script calls Cloudflare.handoff with instructions for the human operator and waits for a Cloudflare.handoffComplete event, replacing the need to manually poll for completion. Refer to the Human in the Loop documentation for examples and best practices.

item.title: Browser Run - New endpoint: /accessibilityTree
item.description: • Added the /accessibilityTree endpoint to capture the accessibility tree from a rendered webpage. The accessibility tree includes roles, names, values, states, and hierarchy, giving AI agents and automation workflows a structured view of page elements without parsing raw HTML or interpreting screenshots. You can capture the full page tree, return only semantically meaningful nodes with interestingOnly, or capture a subtree with root.

item.title: Browser Run - New tutorial: Pre-render pages for crawlers
item.description: • Added a new tutorial on how to pre-render JavaScript-heavy pages using Browser Run and a Worker. The tutorial covers building a pre-rendering endpoint that calls the /content Quick Action to render pages in managed headless Chrome and return crawler-ready HTML for search crawlers, social preview bots, AI indexing jobs, or partner integrations.

item.title: Browser Run - New formats parameter for /snapshot
item.description: • The /snapshot endpoint now supports a formats parameter that lets you return multiple page formats in a single API call. Previously, /snapshot returned only HTML content and a screenshot. You can now also include Markdown and the accessibility tree in the same response. Refer to the /snapshot documentation for usage examples and accepted values.

item.title: Browser Run - Use Quick Actions directly from Workers
item.description: • You can now call Quick Actions directly from a Worker using the quickAction() method on the browser binding. This removes the need for API tokens or external HTTP requests when using Quick Actions within Workers. Supported actions include screenshot, PDF, content, markdown, JSON, scrape, links, and snapshot. The quickAction() method requires a compatibility date of 2026-03-24 or later.

item.title: Browser Run - @cloudflare/playwright v1.3.0 released
item.description: • Released version 1.3.0 of @cloudflare/playwright. Starting with this version, the library uses the standard CDP (Chrome DevTools Protocol) internally to communicate with Browser Run, replacing the previous chunked protocol. This aligns with Browser Run's full CDP support and prevents compatibility issues when using the latest compatibility dates. If you encounter any issues, you can downgrade by setting a compatibility_date prior to 2026-03-17 or by adding the no_websocket_standard_binary_type flag. Refer to the @cloudflare/playwright README for details.

item.title: Browser Run - Higher concurrency limits
item.description:
• Increased the default concurrent browser limit for Workers Paid plans from 30 to 120 per account.
  • Increased new browser instance rate for Workers Paid plans from 30 per minute to 1 per second.
  • Rate limits across the limits page are now expressed in per-second terms, matching how they are enforced.

item.title: Browser Run - Live View
item.description: • Live View lets you see and interact with a remote browser session in real time. Use it to debug automation scripts, monitor what a browser is doing, or manually step in when a task requires human intervention. Access Live View from the Cloudflare dashboard, via the hosted UI at live.browser.run, or using native Chrome DevTools.

item.title: Browser Run - Human in the Loop
item.description: • Human in the Loop lets a human step into a live browser session to handle what automation cannot, such as login pages, CAPTCHAs, or sensitive data entry, then hand control back to the script. Access any active session through Live View.

item.title: Browser Run - Session Recordings
item.description: • Session Recordings captures DOM changes, mouse and keyboard events, and page navigation as structured data so you can replay any browser session after it ends. Enable recordings by passing recording: true when launching a browser. After the session closes, access recordings from the Runs tab in the Cloudflare dashboard or retrieve them via API.

item.title: Browser Run - WebMCP support
item.description: • Browser Run now supports WebMCP (Web Model Context Protocol), which allows websites to declare structured tools that AI agents can discover and execute. WebMCP-enabled browsers are available through the experimental lab browser pool.

item.title: Browser Run - Wrangler CLI commands for Browser Rendering
item.description: • Added wrangler browser commands to create, manage, and view browser sessions directly from the terminal. Available commands: create, close, list, and view. For full usage details, refer to Wrangler commands.

item.title: Browser Run - @cloudflare/puppeteer v1.1.0 released
item.description: • Released version 1.1.0 of @cloudflare/puppeteer, which replaces the internal chunked protocol with plain CDP. This fixes a compatibility issue when using the latest compatibility dates.

item.title: Browser Run - Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) and MCP client support
item.description: • Browser Rendering now exposes the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) as an endpoint. Any CDP-compatible client, including Puppeteer and Playwright, can connect from any environment, whether that is Cloudflare Workers, your local machine, or a cloud environment. MCP clients like Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenCode can also use Browser Rendering as their remote browser.

item.title: Browser Run - Local development: headful mode (experimental)
item.description: • You can now run Chrome in visible (headful) mode during local development by setting X_BROWSER_HEADFUL=true before running wrangler dev or vite dev. This makes it easier to visually debug your browser automation scripts. This feature is experimental and may change without notice.

item.title: Browser Run - @cloudflare/playwright v1.2.0 released
item.description: • Released version 1.2.0 of @cloudflare/playwright, now upgraded to Playwright v1.58.2.

item.title: Browser Run - Separate bot detection IDs for Browser Rendering methods
item.description: • Browser Rendering now uses separate bot detection IDs for the REST API and Browser Sessions versus the crawl endpoint, allowing you to identify and control each method independently. For the full list of IDs, refer to Automatic request headers.

item.title: Browser Run - New REST API endpoint: /crawl (Beta)
item.description: • Added the /crawl endpoint (beta) to the REST API. The /crawl endpoint scrapes content from a starting URL and follows links across the site, up to a configurable depth or page limit. Responses can be returned as HTML, Markdown, or structured JSON (powered by Workers AI).

item.title: Browser Run - Increased REST API rate limits
item.description: • Increased REST API rate limits for Workers Paid plans from 180 requests per minute (3 per second) to 600 requests per minute (10 per second). No action is needed to benefit from the higher limits.

item.title: Browser Run - New tutorial: Generate OG images for Astro sites
item.description: • Added a new tutorial on how to generate OG images for Astro sites using Browser Rendering. The tutorial walks through creating an Astro template, using Browser Rendering to screenshot it as a PNG, and serving the generated images.

item.title: Browser Run - Documentation updates for robots.txt and sitemaps
item.description: • Added robots.txt and sitemaps reference page with guidance on configuring robots.txt and sitemaps for sites accessed by Browser Rendering, including sitemap index files and caching headers.

item.title: Browser Run - @cloudflare/playwright v1.1.1 released
item.description: • Released version 1.1.1 of @cloudflare/playwright, which includes a bug fix that resolves a chunking issue that could occur when generating large PDFs. Upgrade to this version to avoid this issue.

item.title: Browser Run - @cloudflare/puppeteer v1.0.6 released
item.description: • Released version 1.0.6 of @cloudflare/puppeteer, which includes a fix for rendering large text PDFs.

item.title: Browser Run - @cloudflare/puppeteer v1.0.5 released
item.description: • Released version 1.0.5 of @cloudflare/puppeteer, which includes a performance optimization for base64 decoding.

item.title: Browser Run - @cloudflare/playwright v1.1.0 released
item.description: • Released version 1.1.0 of @cloudflare/playwright, now upgraded to Playwright v1.57.0.

item.title: Browser Run - Bug fixes for JSON endpoint, waitForSelector timeout, and WebSocket rendering
item.description:
• Updated the /json endpoint fallback model and improved error handling for when plan limits of Workers Free plan users are reached.
  • REST API requests using waitForSelector will now correctly fail if the specified selector is not found within the time limit.
  • Fixed an issue where pages using WebSockets were not rendering correctly.

item.title: Browser Run - Added guidance on allowlisting Browser Rendering in Bot Management
item.description: • Added FAQ guidance on how to create a WAF skip rule to allowlist Browser Rendering requests when using Bot Management on your zone.

item.title: Browser Run - Improved AI JSON response parsing and debugging
item.description:
• Added rawAiResponse field to /json endpoint error responses, allowing you to inspect the unparsed AI output when JSON parsing fails for easier debugging.
  • Improved AI response handling to better distinguish between valid JSON objects, arrays, and invalid payloads, increasing type safety and reliability.

item.title: Browser Run - Added guidance on REST API timeouts and custom fonts
item.description:
• Added REST API timeouts page explaining how Browser Rendering uses independent timers (for page load, selectors, and actions) and how to configure them.
  • Updated Supported fonts guide with instructions on using your own custom fonts via addStyleTag() in Playwright or Puppeteer.

item.title: Browser Run - Updates to Playwright, new support for Stagehand, and increased limits
item.description:
• Playwright support in Browser Rendering is now GA. We've upgraded to Playwright v1.55.
  • Added support for Stagehand, an open source browser automation framework, powered by Workers AI. Stagehand enables developers to build more reliably and flexibly by combining code with natural-language instructions.
  • Increased limits for paid plans on both the REST API and Browser Sessions.

item.title: Browser Run - Added `excludeExternalLinks` parameter to `/links` REST endpoint
item.description: • Added excludeExternalLinks parameter when using the /links endpoint. When set to true, links pointing to outside the domain of the requested URL are excluded.

item.title: Browser Run - Added `X-Browser-Ms-Used` response header
item.description: • Each REST API response now includes the X-Browser-Ms-Used response header, which reports the browser time (in milliseconds) used by the request.

item.title: Browser Run - Browser Rendering billing goes live
item.description: • Billing for Browser Rendering begins today, August 20th, 2025. See pricing page for full details. You can monitor usage via the Cloudflare dashboard.

item.title: Browser Run - Wrangler updates to local dev
item.description: • Improved the local development experience by updating the method for downloading the dev mode browser and added support for /v1/sessions endpoint, allowing you to list open browser rendering sessions. Upgrade to wrangler@4.31.0 to get started.

item.title: Browser Run - Updates to Playwright, local dev support, and REST API
item.description:
• Playwright upgraded to Playwright v1.54.1 and Playwright MCP upgraded to be in sync with upstream Playwright MCP v0.0.30.
  • Local development with npx wrangler dev now supports Playwright when using Browser Rendering. Upgrade to the latest version of wrangler to get started.
  • The /content endpoint now returns the page's title, making it easier to identify pages.
  • The /json endpoint now allows you to specify your own AI model for the extraction, using the custom_ai parameter.
  • The default viewport size on the /screenshot endpoint has been increased from 800x600 to 1920x1080. You can still override the viewport via request options.

item.title: Browser Run - @cloudflare/puppeteer 1.0.4 released
item.description: • We have released version 1.0.4 of @cloudflare/puppeteer, now in sync with Puppeteer v22.13.1.

item.title: Browser Run - Playwright now supported in local development
item.description: • You can now use Playwright with local development. Upgrade to wrangler@4.26.0 to get started.

item.title: Browser Run - Pricing update to Browser Rendering
item.description: • Billing for Browser Rendering starts on August 20, 2025, with usage beyond the included limits charged according to the new pricing rates.

item.title: Browser Run - Local development support
item.description: • We added local development support to Browser Rendering, making it simpler than ever to test and iterate before deploying.

item.title: Browser Run - New Web Bot Auth headers
item.description: • Browser Rendering now supports Web Bot Auth by automatically attaching Signature-agent, Signature, and Signature-input headers to verify that a request originates from Cloudflare Browser Rendering.

item.title: Browser Run - Bug fix to debug log noise in Workers
item.description: • Fixed an issue where all debug logging was on by default and would flood logs. Debug logs is now off by default but can be re-enabled by setting process.env.DEBUG when needed.

item.title: Browser Run - Playwright MCP
item.description: • You can now deploy Playwright MCP and use any MCP client to get AI models to interact with Browser Rendering.

item.title: Browser Run - Automatic Request Headers
item.description: • Clarified Automatic Request headers in Browser Rendering. These headers are unique to Browser Rendering, and are automatically included and cannot be removed or overridden.

item.title: Browser Run - New free tier and REST API GA with additional endpoints
item.description:
• Browser Rendering now has a new free tier.
  • The REST API is Generally Available.
  • Released new endpoints /json, /links, and /markdown.

item.title: Browser Run - Playwright support
item.description: • You can now use Playwright's browser automation capabilities from Cloudflare Workers.

item.title: Browser Run - New Browser Rendering REST API
item.description: • Released a new REST API in open beta. Available to all customers with a Workers Paid Plan.

item.title: Browser Run - Increased limits
item.description: • Increased the limits on the number of concurrent browsers, and browsers per minute from 2 to 10.

item.title: Browser Run - Update puppeteer to 21.1.0
item.description: • Rebased the fork on the original implementation up till version 21.1.0

item.title: Browser Run - Browser Rendering Available for everyone
item.description: • Browser Rendering is now out of beta and available to all customers with Workers Paid Plan. Analytics and logs are available in Cloudflare's dashboard, under "Worker & Pages".

item.title: Browser Run - Browser Rendering Beta
item.description: • Beta Launch
